changelog._extraSurfacesNote: This repo has the most changelog surfaces in the suite — three. Before 2026-07-31 the gate checked only CHANGELOG.md, so a release could pass green with the other two stale. v0.27.16 and v0.27.17 exist because exactly that drift accumulated to 17 missing versions.

extraSurfaces.note: Served copy. Keep byte-identical — copy the root file, do not hand-edit both.
In-app changelog rendered by ChangelogTab. Items are JSX, not strings, so a new entry must be authored as <>...</> fragments — see the existing entries. Do NOT copy markdown in verbatim.

_claudeMdNote: CLAUDE.md is gitignored, so the release checklist's consistency grep could never see version drift inside it — and this file sat at 0.21.1 / 'May 5, 2026' while the repo was at 0.27.13, THIRTEEN releases stale. Both `**Current Version:**` lines are checked. The `**Last Updated:**` line carries a date, not a version, so it cannot be machine-checked against package.json — update it by hand. Historical prose naming an old release is correct as written and is deliberately not matched. Skipped in CI, where the file is never checked out.

commands.name: lint
commands._note: Cognitive-complexity ratchet (eslint-plugin-sonarjs 4.0.3, threshold 15, whole repo). GATE ON THE NUMBER, NOT THE EXIT CODE — `npm run lint` exits non-zero at an accepted baseline and that is correct; expectProblems is the single place the number lives. AT TRUE ZERO, DELETE THIS KEY — do not set it to 0: at zero findings ESLint emits no problem-count line at all (measured v0.28.4: 0 bytes of output), so shipgate.mjs's `expectProblems` branch hits its `count === null` guard and fails with 'could not read a problem count', naming neither complexity nor the fix. WHOLE REPO rather than a pure-logic core, because the function-level cut at v0.28.5 found no complex-and-untested code here: 0 dark functions, 0 thin, all 13 executed, minimum 6 hits. That is what a low-coverage codebase looks like: spert-story-map's own shipgate.config.json records 9 of its 22 accepted findings in files with no test coverage at all. The condition is absent here. A narrow scope is also a bet on where churn lands, which is unmakeable pre-1.0 — and the core boundary excludes src/features/chart, which holds the two worst findings (cx 105 and 89), while src/shared/storage contributes zero. Baseline 13 is mid-range for the suite. Like-for-like repos — same single rule, same threshold 15 — are Forecaster 9, MyScrumBudget 13, Story Map 22. Scheduler's 3 is measured against sonarjs.configs.recommended, a broader ruleset with rules selectively disabled, so it is not a comparable figure. Zero is NOT the target; refactoring purely to satisfy a threshold is the wrong trade.

commands.name: typecheck
commands._note: Catches type errors in files `next build` never typechecks — tests, and anything else outside the production import graph. Three TS2802 errors sat in `src/lib/__tests__/` from v0.27.15 (c4e174a, the ship-gate install itself) to v0.28.2 with every gate step green, because vitest transpiles without typechecking and `next build` only walks the production graph. Falsified at v0.28.2: an injected TS2322 in a test file fails `npm run typecheck` and passes `npm run build`. This step also needs `src/types/css.d.ts` — without it tsc only passes when a previous `next build` has left a gitignored next-env.d.ts in the tree, so it passed locally and failed on a fresh CI checkout. See that file.

commands.name: build (next build — production graph only)
commands._note: `next build` runs tsc over the production build graph ONLY. Test files are outside that graph and are NOT covered here — that is what the `typecheck` step above is for. Do not delete it as redundant. This note previously claimed types were ‘covered by the build here’, which is how three TS2802 errors in `src/lib/__tests__/` stayed green for six releases.
